newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends firm amid Egypt, Pakistan deals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends firm amid Egypt, Pakistan deals.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mostly firm on the potential for sales of U.S. wheat to Egypt and Pakistan, traders said.

Wheat rallied early this week on news Egypt bought U.S. wheat and there was talk Egypt this weekend may purchase another 500,000 to one million tonnes. Also there are prospects for Pakistan Monday to buy wheat from the U.S. in its tender for 500,000 tonnes of optional-origin supplies.
Export sources said Pakistan may buy up to 250,000 tonnes of U.S. white wheat during Monday's tender.

U.S. exporters also said Friday Egypt may shun U.S. wheat purchases this week after the sharp rally early this week but also pointed out that U.S. supplies remained competitively priced despite the gains in CBOT futures prices.
CBOT wheat futures traders remained cautious.
"Egypt will be a no go. I just talked to my cash sources and there's been no bid," a cash-connected trader said.
But Cargill Inc bought two million bushels of September, LIT America, Merrill Lynch Futures, R.J. O'Brien, Paine Webber and Rosenthal Collins each bought two million December.
Wheat closed one cent higher to two cents lower, with September unchanged at $3.58-1/2.
Wheat spread dealings were nearly non-existent with LIT America doing a light amount of September/December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 14,500 contracts, below the 21,360 traded Thursday.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures sold 600 December $3.90 puts at 31 to 33-1/4 cents, E.D. and F. Man interntional sold 300 December $3.80 calls at 18 cents and sold 300 December $3.70 calls at 22-1/2 to 23 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, below the 10,761 traded Thursday.
